title: Shakespeare's Works and Legacy
text: William Shakespeare (1564–1616) is widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language and the world's greatest dramatist. He wrote approximately 39 plays, 154 sonnets, and several longer poems. His works, including Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, King Lear, Romeo and Juliet, A Midsummer Night's Dream, and The Tempest, have been translated into every major language and are performed more often than those of any other playwright. Shakespeare was a part-owner of the Globe Theatre in London. His works explore themes of love, jealousy, power, ambition, and mortality with psychological depth and linguistic innovation. An estimated 1,700 words in English are first recorded in Shakespeare's texts.
